Subject: Private Offer: SKU thresholds that trigger discounts + reseller commission question

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier. Cloudbridge is preparing a private offer run rate for 2029 and we want to structure the PO so that incremental SKU thresholds trigger deeper list discounts (e.g., >$250k/mo = +5% off list). Two quick asks: 1) can Redwood support conditional tiering in a single private offer (thresholds by SKU group, not just total ARR)? 2) how do you typically handle channel/reseller commissions on private offers — do you allow a full pass-through of committed discount to the reseller, or do you retain a small holdback for reconciliations?

Attached is our SOW draft for context (Cloudbridge_SOW_v1.pdf). We also need to understand timing: Cloudbridge prefers a staged phasing (Q3 soft-launch, Q4 full commit). Any flexibility on upfront credits for the first partial year?

Goal: get a proposed structure and a rough margin/commission waterfall to present to procurement next week.

Thanks,
Jared Miller
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Cloudbridge

Jared — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High level response below; attaching an internal sketched private-offer flow for ops (Redwood_PO_Strat_v1.pdf).

1) Conditional tiering: yes — we can model SKU-group thresholds within a single PO. We recommend a three-band approach (Baseline, Growth, Accelerator) that map to monthly usage bands by SKU group so the list discount increases as Cloudbridge crosses each band.

2) Reseller commission/pass-through: our standard is to allow reseller pass-through but with a 1.5–3% reconciliation holdback depending on tax/finance treatment and whether the reseller is authorized for direct billing. For a large, multi-region account like Cloudbridge I would propose an 8% gross reseller commission with a 2% holdback that is reconciled after quarterly true-ups.

3) Phasing & credits: staged phasing is fine. For the soft-launch (Q3) we can provide a one-time usage credit equal to 20% of expected Q3 usage capped at $150k; for full Q4 commitment we will honor the tiers retroactively. Upfront cash credits are possible but will reduce pass-through commission on a pro-rata basis.

Next steps: I want to align internally on the commission waterfall and tax treatment; Soojin/ Iren e — can you weigh in on holdback size and whether the ops team can implement SKU-bound thresholds within one PO (billing + metering)?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Cloud Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Inline comments from ops/partnerships:
- Holdback: recommend 1% holdback for ACP-authorized resellers, 2% for non-authorized. For Cloudbridge (large, audited partner) 1% seems defensible — keeps the commission attractive while protecting against overbilling.
- Commission ladder: propose 6% base up to band 1, 9% for band 2, 12% for accelerator band. We can cap commission payout per SKU to avoid gaming where a low-price SKU is used to drive higher % payouts.
- Credits: recommend offering the Q3 soft-launch credit as a usage credit (non-cash) to avoid tax complications; allow a one-time cash offset only if Cloudbridge agrees to extended commit.

Operational ask: Irene — can the metering pipeline apply band lookups per SKU group and return effective discount codes at billing time? If not, we need to split the PO into two linked offers (ugh).

Happy to sync on the numbers if you want a quick call.

— Soojin

Priya — thanks, this is helpful and closer to what procurement needs. A few points before we take to the exec committee: 

• Commission: Cloudbridge prefers a simpler %-of-revenue pass-through for the reseller; can we commit to the 9% blended across bands as a floor (instead of tiered payout), with a 1% holdback returned after quarterly true-ups? That helps our reseller economics and reduces complexity internally.
• Q3 credit: to smooth the soft-launch risk we are asking for a 30% upfront usage credit for year one (applied across SKU groups) rather than a capped $150k — this reduces Cloudbridge cash burn during integration.
• SLA / credits: procurement will ask about tighter SLAs for multi-region failover and specific outage credit schedules. Will Redwood entertain a partial SLA carve for this private offer?

If you can confirm the 9% blended pass-through and the 30% upfront usage credit (non-refundable credit applied against invoices), we can sign the attached PO and start DocuSign. I attached an internal procurement template (we referenced your earlier slides).

Appreciate the collaboration — Jared
